_meta.purpose: SAFETY_MINIMUM records. These are food-safety floors from USDA FSIS (and FDA for seafood). They are not preferences and no other record may present a lower figure as safe. USDA/FSIS wins every conflict.
_meta.rendering_rule: Every surface that prints any temperature for an animal must print that animal's SAFETY_MINIMUM alongside it, name USDA FSIS as the source, and state the rest time where one applies. Colour is never proof of safety.

records.rest: at least 3 minutes before carving or consuming
records.measurement: food thermometer in the thickest part, away from bone, fat and gristle, read before removing from the heat source
records.statement: Cook all raw beef, pork, lamb, goat and veal steaks, chops and roasts to a minimum internal temperature of 145 F (62.8 C) and allow to rest for at least 3 minutes.
notes: Fresh pork at 145 F can still be pink in the centre and is safe (FSIS).
Consumers may choose higher temperatures for personal preference; lower is not safe.

records.scope: ground meat, burgers, sausage mixtures, meat loaf, and organ or variety meats
records.measurement: food thermometer through the side of a patty to the centre
records.statement: Cook ground beef, pork, lamb, goat and veal, and all organ and variety meats, to 160 F (71.1 C).
notes: One in four hamburgers that look done may not be safely cooked (FSIS).

records.scope: breasts, whole bird, legs, thighs, wings, ground poultry, giblets and stuffing
records.measurement: for a whole bird, check the innermost part of the thigh and wing and the thickest part of the breast
records.statement: Cook all poultry, including ground poultry, giblets and stuffing, to 165 F (73.9 C).
notes: USDA does not require a rest for poultry. Two of the ChatGPT masters print '165 F with a 3 minute rest' for chicken; the rest is not USDA guidance and is recorded as a graphics defect.
Pink colour in safely cooked chicken can come from heat-stable hemoglobin, and smoking or grilling makes it more likely in young birds (FSIS).
Never pull poultry below 165 F to rely on carryover. Carryover is not a safety mechanism.

records.measurement: thermometer in the thickest part of the fillet; or the flesh is opaque and separates easily with a fork
records.statement: Cook fish and shellfish to 145 F (62.8 C), or until the flesh is opaque and separates easily with a fork.
notes: Salmon served below 145 F (the common 120 to 135 F preference range) is a culinary preference below the federal minimum and must be labelled as such wherever it appears.

records.scope: fresh ham, or smoked ham sold uncooked
records.statement: Cook fresh or smoked (uncooked) ham to 145 F (62.8 C) and allow to rest for at least 3 minutes.
Reheat fully cooked ham to 165 F (73.9 C). A ham packaged in a USDA-inspected plant may be reheated to 140 F (60 C).
notes: Master pork-B prints 'Reheat to 140 F or until hot' for ham with no plant qualifier. That is only correct for USDA-inspected-plant packaged ham; recorded as a graphics defect.

records.scope: leftovers and casseroles, including reheated smoked meat
records.statement: Reheat leftovers and casseroles to 165 F (73.9 C).
notes: Refrigerate smoked meat within 2 hours of removing it from the smoker; use within 4 days or freeze (FSIS).

records.statement: Cook egg dishes to 160 F (71.1 C).
notes: Kept so the master temperature reference page can print the full FSIS chart without omission.
